rationale: The quality leg (oancf − ni) is the canonical Sloan accruals anomaly merely rescaled by total liabilities, and the composite is a near-cosmetic variant of the archive's already-tested cash-to-market × operating-cash-quality signals (Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount, Self-Financed Cash Discount).

The quality leg (oancf − dp)/lt is byte-for-byte the one already tested in "Maintenance-Covered Earnings Yield," so this is a leg-swap recombination of two archived signals (that one and "After-Payout Liability Cover Yield") rather than a new mechanism.

It is internally consistent and genuinely motivated by the fmb/alpha sign conflict in the earlier net-current-asset EBITDA signal by replacing a liquidity-buffer reward with a cash-conversion efficiency test, though the act + lct denominator is an ad hoc gross-working-capital scalar whose economic interpretation is weaker than net working capital or sales.

This repeats the already-tested "Accelerating-Asset-Wear Book Trap" / depreciation-intensity theme with only a level-vs-acceleration and denominator change, and scaling dp by gross profit (which can be near zero or negative) makes the conditioning variable numerically unstable despite winsorization.

It is a component swap inside the archive's best-performing construction (che-to-market × SUMRANK quality composite), substituting ni/revt for oancf/revt and re/lt for −cogs/revt, both of which already appear as quality legs elsewhere in the archive, so it tests no new economic channel.

The expression matches the stated negative-sign hypothesis and pairs a sales-yield anchor with a post-maintenance cash-burn leg not previously combined in the archive, but the "trap" framing is largely presentational since the leg is just the sign-flipped coverage ratio proposed elsewhere in this same batch, making the two proposals partially redundant.
